references.text: Describes the same situation where a Hebrew slave declares his love for his master and chooses to remain in service permanently, instead of going free.
Provides the background for the release of Hebrew slaves in the seventh year, which is the context for Deuteronomy 15:16.
Addresses the treatment of Israelite servants and the principle of release, related to the theme of slaves who choose to remain with their master.
Expresses a similar theme of willing service and obedience, where the servant declares his joy in doing God's will.
Describes foreigners who hold fast to the Lord's covenant and choose to serve Him out of love.
